title: DXF R2000+ boolean HEADER group-290 reimport/reexport compatibility

observation.failure: The selected IMAGEDEF/IMAGEDEF_REACTOR ASCII and Binary reimport matrix failed when reexporting an AC1018 DXF at HEADER initial validation.
observation.cause: The writer emits EXTNAMES, PSTYLEMODE, and OLESTARTUP using boolean group code 290 for versions after AC1014, but the initial preflight accepted group 290 only for versions after AC1021.
observation.support_boundary: Autodesk's DXF HEADER reference documents EXTNAMES and PSTYLEMODE as group 290; the group-code type reference defines 290-299 as boolean values. This evidence supports code admission and roundtrip consistency, not native feature semantics.

implementation.change: Accept group 290 for these HEADER booleans from AC1015 onward while retaining group 70 for the packed DWG/legacy representation. Group 290 remains refused for AC1014.
implementation.related_test_adjustment: The generated native-DWG selector now asserts that the known incomplete AC1027 source profile is refused for ASCII and Binary output with no raster proof published. It does not count this profile as a successful output cell.

sources.title: HEADER Section Group Codes (DXF)
sources.supports: EXTNAMES and PSTYLEMODE use group code 290.

sources.title: Group Code Value Types Reference (DXF)
sources.supports: Group codes 290-299 are boolean flag values.

validation.coverage: Accept group 290 for AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, and AC1032; reject it for AC1014.
12 generated ASCII/Binary revision reimports and reexports; 10 successful local DWG-source cells; two AC1027 incomplete-source refusal controls; atomic mutation/refusal/retry checks.

fixture_policy: No DWG or DXF fixture files were added; all generated controls use scratch paths.
limitations: Generated same-library codec consistency is not independent producer or native-consumer qualification.
AC1027 DWG output remains refused when source references are not fully qualified.
The IMAGEDEF owner back-reference output gate remains in force; P6-A remains open.
